applicableAreas: Biofiltration/detention pond area in northeastern portion of site
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) identified the biofiltration/detention pond in the northeastern corner adjacent to the eastern property boundary. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows overhead electric line ('-OHE-') along the western boundary of the site, not near the water quality features. No overhead distribution conductors are explicitly shown in proximity to the detention pond location. The plans show the pond is approximately 44+ feet from buildings based on dimension annotations. However, the specific horizontal sky-to-ground clearance distance between any overhead distribution primary, neutral, or secondary conductors and the water's edge of the detention pond is not dimensioned or calculated on the plans.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.1 applicability requires water quality features to be proposed on sites WITH overhead distribution facilities within clearance distance. While the site has overhead electric infrastructure (on the western boundary per Sheet 21 vision analysis), the detention pond is located in the northeastern area, separated by the entire width of the development. The plans do not show any overhead distribution lines in the vicinity of the pond, nor do they provide clearance calculations demonstrating the required 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance. Without profile views, engineer-sealed clearance documentation, or explicit callouts showing conductor locations relative to the pond, the specific clearance cannot be verified from available evidence. This is marked 'unclear' rather than 'fail' because the overhead line may be distant enough to comply, but documentation is insufficient to confirm compliance.
findings.comment: No engineer-sealed profile or elevation drawing shows clearance verification between overhead distribution conductors and the water's edge of the detention pond. If overhead distribution lines are present within 15 feet of the pond, minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance must be demonstrated with dimensioned drawings.

findings.observation: Review of all submitted site plan sheets (Sheets 1-39) identified no engineer-sealed profile plans, section exhibits, or elevation views showing clearance verification between the detention pond and electric facilities. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows the site plan layout with electrical infrastructure but is not a profile view and includes no clearance dimension callouts. Sheets 15 and 16 show biofiltration pond details and profiles but do not show any overlay or comparison with electrical conductor locations or provide clearance verification with electric facility dimensions. No cross-referenced detail showing vertical or horizontal clearances between pond features and electric lines is present in the documented submittal.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.7 explicitly requires 'engineer-scaled section exhibits, or elevation views showing clearance verification and dimensions between water quality features (detention ponds, rain gardens, bioswales) and electric facilities.' The code citation UCM § 1.10.3 requires these clearance documents where features are proposed within 15 feet of overhead conductors. Although general site plans are provided, the specific engineer-sealed profile sections with clearance dimensions are missing. This is a documentation deficiency.
findings.comment: Provide professional engineer-sealed profile plans and elevation drawings showing horizontal and vertical clearances between the detention pond boundaries and all electric facilities (overhead conductors, poles, underground transformers, pull boxes, conduits). Dimensions must demonstrate compliance with applicable clearance minimums.

applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern and southern property boundaries
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) identified the concrete retaining wall enclosing the biofiltration/detention pond located in the northeastern corner. The vision tool analysis explicitly states: 'Yes, the Biofiltration/Detention Pond overlaps. The eastern edge of the "Concrete Retaining Wall" enclosing the pond is drawn completely within the 5-foot space between the dashed easement line and the eastern property line.' This retaining wall is a permanent improvement structure (not an electric facility) within the 5' electric easement boundary. The plat (Sheet 2) labels 5' electric easements along property boundaries. The site plan shows the retaining wall within this 5-foot zone.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 and the grouping description state: 'No permanent structures, buildings, swimming pools, or improvements (including below-grade footings) are allowed within electric easements.' A concrete retaining wall is explicitly a permanent improvement. The vision analysis confirmed it is within the 5' electric easement. The fundamental prohibition applies: no permanent structures above or below grade in electric easements are permitted.
findings.comment: Concrete retaining wall enclosing the detention pond is located within the 5' Electric Easement and must be removed or relocated outside the easement. No permanent structures are permitted within electric easements where Austin Energy must maintain 24-hour access to facilities.

applicableAreas: Biofiltration/detention pond area and eastern property boundary within 5' Electric Easement
findings.observation: Sheet 16 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles) maintenance requirements specify: 'No unvegetated area shall exceed ten (10) square feet. This performance requirement applies to the entire pond including the pond bottom, side slopes, and areas adjacent to the pond.' The pond requires 95% vegetative cover per biweekly maintenance inspections in the first growing season. Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed the pond is located within the 5' Electric Easement along the eastern boundary. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) shows the pond area and adjacent landscape features but contains no indication of a license agreement with Austin Energy Public Involvement. No document references or site plan notes state 'obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement' regarding landscaping authorization within the easement. The absence of a filed license agreement is the deficiency.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires: 'A license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is required before installing any landscaping or irrigation that might obstruct access to facilities within electric easements.' The grouping description clarifies: 'Plans showing landscaping within easements must demonstrate the license agreement has been "obtained from and filed with" Austin Energy Public Involvement—not "to be obtained." Missing license agreements result in certificate of occupancy holds.' The detention pond's required vegetation (95% cover) constitutes landscaping within the electric easement. The submitted plans provide no evidence that an executed license agreement has been obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement.
findings.comment: The detention pond with required vegetation is located within the 5' Electric Easement but no executed license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is documented on the plans. Obtain and file license agreement with Austin Energy authorizing landscaping and vegetation within the easement, or relocate pond outside easement boundary.

applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirms the detention pond retaining wall is within the 5' Electric Easement. Sheet 16 specifies the pond requires vegetation maintenance with 95% cover and detailed biweekly and routine maintenance. Vision analysis of Sheet 31 shows trees in the eastern boundary area near the pond. The concrete retaining wall physically encloses the pond area. While the landscape plan shows some access routes and a maintenance gate (per Sheet 16 details), the required vegetation within the pond and the concrete retaining wall infrastructure would obstruct free vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance trucks and equipment to traverse the easement. The retaining wall and pond infrastructure are permanent features that occupy and restrict the 24/7 vehicular access corridor.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 requires that 'landscaping within easements must maintain 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment.' A concrete retaining wall enclosing a pond, combined with required dense vegetation (95% cover), creates a physical obstruction preventing free vehicular access across the easement. The maintenance requirements (routine vegetation trimming, inspections, replacement) also require Austin Energy to navigate around or within the landscaped pond area. This setup does not maintain unobstructed access.
findings.comment: The detention pond with required vegetation and concrete retaining walls within the 5' Electric Easement obstructs required 24/7 vehicular access for Austin Energy maintenance. Relocate pond outside the easement or demonstrate 24-foot minimum clear drivable surface for maintenance vehicle access across the easement width.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) vision analysis identified multiple utility easements: wastewater easement, drainage easements, public utility easement, and electric easements. Sheets 19-20 (Utility Tap Plans) show water meter and wastewater connection points on the western side of the property. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric transformers at locations: NW corner Bldg. 1, SW corner Bldg. 8, SE corner Bldg. 6, and between Bldgs. 4-5. The utility tap locations (water meter) do not appear to be within the 5' electric easement on the eastern boundary based on their western-side positioning. However, no explicit statement is provided on the plans confirming that all utility equipment (water meters, backflow preventers, wastewater connection points) are located outside the electric easements.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.13 requires: 'Water, wastewater, or gas utility facilities, meters, vaults, backflow preventers, valves, tanks, or equipment located within electric easements where only electric facilities are permitted.' The plans show utility infrastructure locations but do not explicitly confirm that all non-electric utility equipment is outside the electric easement boundaries. While visual inspection suggests water/wastewater connections are on the western side away from the eastern electric easement, explicit clearance confirmation with dimension callouts is absent. Marked 'unclear' because the issue cannot be definitively confirmed from available plan evidence.
findings.comment: Provide utility plan with explicit confirmation and dimensions showing that all water meters, wastewater connection points, backflow preventers, and other utility equipment are located outside all electric easements and crossing utility lines cross only perpendicularly.

applicableAreas: Biofiltration/detention pond in northeastern corner within 5' Electric Easement
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 explicitly confirmed: 'Yes, the Biofiltration/Detention Pond overlaps. The eastern edge of the "Concrete Retaining Wall" enclosing the pond is drawn completely within the 5-foot space between the dashed easement line and the eastern property line.' Sheet 2 (Plat) shows 5' Electric Easements along property boundaries. Sheets 15-16 detail the detention pond structure and vegetation requirements. The drainage easements shown on Sheet 9 are separate from the electric easements. The detention pond itself, with its retaining walls, biofiltration media, and required vegetation, is located within the 5' Electric Easement along the eastern boundary. This violates the principle that electric easements are reserved exclusively for electric facilities.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.14.4 and § 1.14.7 specify that drainage structures, detention ponds, and other non-electric features are prohibited within electric easements where they would impair Austin Energy's access and maintenance of electric facilities. The submitted plans clearly show the detention pond retaining wall within the 5' electric easement. A detention pond with retaining walls, vegetation, and maintenance requirements is a drainage structure that obstructs the easement and prevents unobstructed access for electric facility maintenance.
findings.comment: The biofiltration/detention pond, including its retaining walls and required vegetation, is located within the 5' Electric Easement and must be relocated outside the easement boundary. Detention ponds cannot be located within electric easements as they obstruct required access and maintenance corridors.

applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) identified: 'Wooden Privacy Fence: A line with 'x' marks runs along the eastern boundary, which corresponds to Key Note "H-6" ("WOODEN PRIVACY FENCE").' The fence is shown running along the eastern property boundary where the 5' Electric Easement is located. The landscape plan does not indicate whether this fence is removable or permanent construction. Standard wood privacy fences are typically permanent installations anchored with set footings.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 allows: 'Removable wooden fences may be allowed in easements under license agreement if removable to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access.' However, non-removable or permanent fencing prevents access. The landscape plan shows a wooden privacy fence along the eastern boundary within the electric easement area but provides no specification indicating it is removable or that a license agreement exists. The deficiency is unclear because the fence material (wood) suggests it might be removable, but the details do not confirm this, and no license agreement documentation is provided.
findings.comment: If wooden privacy fence is located within the 5' Electric Easement, provide detail sheet specifications confirming it is removable and readily can be removed to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access. Alternatively, provide executed license agreement from Austin Energy authorizing the fence installation. Permanent fencing is not permitted in electric easements.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows multiple easements including drainage, wastewater, utility, and electric. Sheets 19-20 (Utility Tap Plans) show water and wastewater service connections. Sheet 21 shows underground electric routing. The utility plans indicate water service connection on the western side and wastewater connection points, suggesting these utilities may cross the site. However, the plans do not show explicit routing alignments or crossing angles for utilities relative to the electric easements. No detail sheets or notes specify the crossing angles or confirm perpendicular crossings of non-electric utilities through electric easements.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.16 requires: 'Non-electric utility lines (water, wastewater, gas, private utilities) running parallel or longitudinally within electric easements rather than crossing perpendicularly.' The code allows perpendicular utility crossings but prohibits parallel runs or utility equipment/vaults within easements. The submitted plans do not explicitly document the routing angles and crossing methodologies for water and wastewater utilities relative to electric easements. Without these details, compliance with the perpendicular crossing requirement cannot be confirmed.
findings.comment: Provide utility coordination plan documenting that all non-electric utilities (water, wastewater) cross electric easements at perpendicular or near-perpendicular angles. Confirm no utility lines run parallel or longitudinally within electric easements and no utility vaults or equipment are located within easement boundaries.

applicableAreas: 5' Electric Easement along eastern property boundary
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 (Site Plan) and Sheet 10 (Fire Protection Plan) identified fire hydrant 1 (FH) located 'directly intersecting the dashed line that marks the inner boundary of the 5' Electric Easement. This places the center of the fire hydrant exactly on the 5-foot mark from the eastern property boundary.' The fire hydrant appears to be partially within the distribution electric easement, not within a transmission easement. UCM § 1.14.7 cited in EL-5.23 specifically addresses transmission easements ('Easements for Transmission Facilities') with a 20-foot minimum clearance requirement from transmission structures.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.23 applicability is 'Only when transmission easements or transmission structures are present and fire hydrants are proposed.' This site has distribution easements and distribution-level infrastructure, not transmission. The cited code (UCM § 1.14.7) is transmission-specific. While fire hydrants should not be located in electric easements generally (per basic access principles), this specific checklist item is transmission-focused. The fire hydrant proximity to the distribution easement boundary is problematic for access but is not captured by EL-5.23's transmission-specific criteria. Marked 'unclear' because the fire hydrant location relative to distribution easements is a potential issue not specifically addressed by EL-5.23.
findings.comment: Fire hydrant is located on or within the 5' Electric Easement boundary. While EL-5.23 is transmission-specific, fire hydrants should be located entirely outside distribution electric easements to prevent obstruction of access. Verify fire hydrant is completely outside all electric easement boundaries.

applicableAreas: Pedestals, vaults, and manhole locations throughout site
findings.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identified four electrical transformer pad locations. These are pad-mounted (surface) units, not subsurface vaults. The plans do not show any underground pedestals, subsurface vaults, or Austin Energy maintenance access points (separate from building-owned transformers). The presence of subsurface Austin Energy electric vaults or pedestals requiring 8-foot personnel access clearance is not indicated on the electrical plans provided.
findings.reasoning: EL-5.25 requires: '8 feet of clearance from pedestals, subsurface Austin Energy vaults, or manholes that require personnel access.' The application shows distribution transformers but does not explicitly show or identify Austin Energy-owned subsurface vaults or pedestals separate from the building service infrastructure. If such Austin Energy infrastructure exists underground, the plans do not depict it. Marked 'unclear' because the actual presence of Austin Energy vaults/pedestals requiring this clearance is not confirmed on available plans.
findings.comment: Provide utility coordination documentation from Austin Energy identifying all subsurface vaults, pedestals, and maintenance access points. Ensure all structures and improvements maintain 8-foot minimum clearance from these access points in all directions.
